Smt. Punam vs Savai Singh on 3 February, 2026
 Neutral Citation No. 2026:Mphc-Ind:3717
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
At Indore

Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Himanshu Joshi

On The 3 rd Of February, 2026
 Misc. Appeal No. 3008 of 2017
 Smt. Punam
 Versus
 Savai Singh And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Manoj Malviya - Advocate on behalf of Shri Romil
 counsel for appellant.

Shri Manoj Jain - Advocate for the respondent No.3.
 Order

The present appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been preferred by the appellant/claimant, challenging the award dated 25.09.2017, passed by the 10th Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Indore in Claim Case No.150/2016, whereby the learned Tribunal partly allowed the claim and awarded compensation amounting to Rs.3,22,500/- along with interest at the rate of 7% per annum.
2.

entities.text: 10th Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Indore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The factual matrix of the case is that on 19.01.2012, Neeraj Khandelwal, husband of applicant Poonam was driving his own car bearing registration No. MP-09-CA-4548 from Ratlam to Indore,
after attending a house-warming ceremony, via Badnawar.
The vehicle was being driven at a moderate speed.

When the car reached Amla Fata on Badnawar Road, the driver of the trailer bearing registration No. RJ-19-GB-8724, the respondent NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-IND:3717 2 MA-3008-2017 No. 2, was driving the said vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and at an excessive speed.
While so driving, the trailer driver suddenly applied brakes without giving any signal or warning.
As a result, the car driven by Neeraj Khandelwal, which was following the trailer, collided with it and met with a severe accident.
In the said accident, Neeraj Khandelwal, Mrs. Sumitra, Mrs. Shashi, Ayush Khandelwal and Parth Khandelwal sustained grievous injuries and succumbed thereto.

The incident was reported at Police Station Badnagar,
where a criminal case was registered against respondent No. 2, the driver of the trailer, under Section 304-A of the IPC.
At the time of the accident, deceased Neeraj Khandelwal was aged about 48 years and was working as an accountant, earning approximately 65,000 per month.
Due to his untimely death, the applicant has been deprived of his income, love, care and companionship.

The appellant/claimant being husband was depending on the income of deceased, therefore, she filed a claim petition under Section 163-A of Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation to the tune of Smt. Punam vs Savai Singh on 3 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/176993902/
1 Rs.25,50,000/- on account of death of Neeraj Khandelwal.
3. Learned claims Tribunal found that the accident was caused due to rash and negligent driving of respondent no.2 which was insured with respondent No.3 on the fateful day.
Thus learned MACT after appreciating the evidence on record partly allowed the claim petition and awarded a sum of Rs.3,22,500/- against the claim of Rs.25,50,000/-.

4. Learned counsel for the appellant argued that the learned Tribunal erred in not awarding the compensation under the head of future prospects as well deducting the compensation giving the finding of contributory NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:3717 3 MA-3008-2017 negligence.
He prays for enhancement of the compensation.

5. Refutting the submissions advanced by learned counsel for the appellant, learned counsel for the respondent submitted that the finding arrived at by the learned tribunal are just and proper and does not require any interference by this Court in this appeal.

6. I have heard the rival submissions of learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
7.
It is not in dispute that respondent No.1 was responsible for causing the accident and the offending vehicle was insured with respondent No.3 on the fateful day.

The only question for determination in this appeal is that whether the amount awarded by the Tribunal requires modification or not and finding given by the Tribunal in respect of contributory negligence is correct or not ?
8.

Considering the submissions made by learned counsel for parties, this Court finds that the learned Tribunal erred in not awarding the compensation under the head of future prospects, and thus the compensation is being reassessed as under :
Loss of dependency :
Annual Income : 60,000/- Future Prospects (25%) : 75,000/- Deduction (1/3) :
50,000/- Multiplier (13) : 6,50,000/-
Consortium : 40,000/-

Funeral Expenses : 15,000/-
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:3717 4 MA-3008-2017 Loss of Estate :
15,000/- Total Compensation : 7,20,000/-
9.
The finding of contributory negligence attributed to the deceased deserves to be reduced from 50% to 25%, as the evidence on record does not justify an equal apportionment of fault.

While it may be contended that the deceased contributed to the occurrence of the accident to a limited extent, the primary and effective cause of the accident squarely lies with the rash and negligent conduct of the other offending vehicle.

The material facts, manner of impact, and surrounding circumstances clearly indicate that the deceased was not the dominant contributor to the accident,
Smt. Punam vs Savai Singh on 3 February, 2026

Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/176993902/
2 and at best, his role was marginal.
In such circumstances, fastening 50% negligence on the deceased is excessive, arbitrary, and contrary to the settled principles governing contributory negligence.

A more reasonable and equitable assessment would be to restrict the contributory negligence to 25%,
thereby ensuring a just and proportionate determination of liability.
10. Accordingly, the claimant is entitled to the get the compensation to the tune of Rs. 5,40,000/- in place of Rs. 3,22,500/-.

The enhanced sum of Rs. 2,17,500/- shall carry the same interest as has been awarded by the learned Tribunal subject to following conditions:-
"i.
The respondent No.3 is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order, failing which the execution can be taken out against him.
ii. The claimant is directed to pay the requisite Court Fee, if required in the present case.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:3717 5 MA-3008-2017 iii.
On such deposit, the claimant is permitted to withdraw the amount with accrued interest and costs, by filing a proper application before the Tribunal.
iv. The record be sent back to the learned Tribunal within three weeks from this day.
v. As a sequel, interlocutory applications pending consideration, if any, shall stand closed vi.
No order as to costs.

(HIMANSHU JOSHI) JUDGE (ra)
